editions.name: The Birth of Venus
editions.note: Venus drifts ashore on a scallop shell, blown in by the west wind. Painted on canvas, still unusual in Florence then, it was one of the first big mythological nudes since antiquity.

editions.name: Girl with a Pearl Earring
editions.note: Not a portrait but a tronie, a Dutch study of a face, here in an exotic turban. The blue is ultramarine, ground from lapis lazuli and pricier than gold.

editions.name: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
editions.at: The Met, New York (one of many impressions)
editions.note: From the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, printed in the thousands. The deep blue is Prussian blue, then a new import to Japan. Fuji sits tiny in the trough of the wave.

editions.name: The Starry Night
editions.note: The view from his window at the asylum in Saint-Rémy just before sunrise, with an invented village and a huge cypress. He painted it from memory, during the day.

editions.name: The Kiss
materials: oil and gold leaf on canvas
editions.note: The peak of his Golden Period: two lovers wrapped in one robe, his side covered in rectangles, hers in circles. The Austrian state bought it right off its first show in 1908.

editions.name: Unique Forms of Continuity in Space
editions.note: A striding figure blurred by speed, the Futurist dream of motion in solid form. Boccioni made it in plaster; the bronzes were cast after he died in 1916. It's on Italy's 20 cent coin.

editions.name: The Two Fridas
editions.at: Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City
editions.note: Painted the year she divorced Diego Rivera: one Frida in a white European dress, one in Tehuana dress, their exposed hearts joined by a single vein. Her largest painting.

editions.name: No. 61 (Rust and Blue)
editions.note: Soft-edged blocks of color floating on a field, meant to be seen up close so they fill your sight. Rothko said people who wept in front of his paintings were having the same experience he had painting them.

editions.name: Infinity Mirrored Room: The Souls of Millions of Light Years Away
editions.note: A small dark room of mirrors and black water hung with hundreds of tiny LED lights that fade in and out, so it seems to go on forever. Visitors get about a minute inside.

editions.name: Maman
editions.note: A spider more than 9 m tall, an ode to her mother, who repaired tapestries. Under its body hangs a sac of marble eggs.

editions.name: Arnolfini Portrait
editions.note: A merchant and his wife in their room in Bruges. The round mirror on the back wall shows two more people in the doorway, maybe the painter, who signed the wall above it: Jan van Eyck was here.

editions.name: The Garden of Earthly Delights
editions.note: A triptych: Eden on the left, a crowded paradise of pleasures in the middle, hell on the right, with a man whose body is a broken eggshell. Nobody agrees on what it means.

editions.name: Mona Lisa
editions.note: Probably Lisa Gherardini, wife of a Florentine silk merchant. Leonardo kept working on it for years and never handed it over. Its fame took off after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911.

editions.name: David
editions.note: Carved from a block of marble other sculptors had given up on, over 5 m tall. David is shown before the fight, sizing up Goliath. The original moved indoors in 1873; a copy stands in the Piazza della Signoria.

editions.name: The School of Athens
editions.note: Plato points up and Aristotle holds his hand flat at the center of a crowd of ancient thinkers. Raphael is said to have given Plato Leonardo's face, and put himself in at the right edge.

editions.name: The Creation of Adam
editions.note: One panel of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, which Michelangelo painted over four years on scaffolding. The two fingers almost touch.

editions.name: Young Hare
editions.note: A hare drawn hair by hair in watercolor, so closely you can see a window reflected in its eye. Rarely shown, to keep it out of the light.

editions.name: The Ambassadors
editions.note: Two French envoys in London among globes, books and instruments. The smear across the floor is a skull painted in stretched perspective: it only snaps into shape when you look from the side.
editions.credit: Hans Holbein the Younger · Public domain

editions.name: The Hunters in the Snow
editions.note: Tired hunters come home with one fox to show for it while people skate on the frozen ponds below. One of six paintings of the times of the year; five survive.
editions.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder · Public domain

editions.name: Pine Trees
editions.note: Pines half lost in mist, in nothing but ink, across two folding screens with more empty paper than trees. A National Treasure of Japan.

editions.name: View of Toledo
editions.note: A storm over the Spanish city where the Greek-born painter lived, with its buildings moved around to suit the picture. One of only two landscapes of his that survive.

editions.name: The Calling of Saint Matthew
editions.note: Christ points at a tax collector counting coins in a dark room, and a beam of light follows his hand. Still in the chapel it was painted for.

editions.name: Judith Slaying Holofernes
editions.note: The biblical widow and her maid pin down the general and cut off his head. Gentileschi painted the scene more than once; this is the later, bloodier version.

editions.name: Apollo and Daphne
editions.note: The nymph turns into a laurel tree the moment the god catches her: bark climbs her legs and her fingers sprout leaves, all in marble. Bernini was in his mid-twenties.

editions.name: Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings
editions.note: The Mughal emperor, haloed by a sun and moon, hands a book to a Sufi sage and ignores an Ottoman sultan and King James I of England waiting below. Bichitr painted himself in the corner.

editions.name: Two Lovers
editions.note: A young couple wrapped in an embrace, in the loose late style of the master of the Isfahan court. Abbasi made single pages for collectors rather than illustrations for books.

editions.name: The Night Watch
editions.note: A civic militia company setting off, painted as a scene in motion instead of a row of faces. It isn't set at night: darkened varnish gave it the name. It was cut down on all sides in 1715 to fit a wall.

editions.name: Las Meninas
editions.note: The little princess with her maids, a dwarf and a dog, and Velázquez himself at a huge canvas. The king and queen appear only in the mirror at the back, as if standing where you are.

editions.name: Irises
materials: ink and color on gold leaf
editions.note: Clumps of blue irises on gold and nothing else, from a scene in The Tales of Ise. Some clumps repeat as if stenciled. A National Treasure, shown each spring when the irises bloom.

editions.name: One Hundred Horses
editions.note: An Italian Jesuit at the Qing court, known in China as Lang Shining, painting a long scroll of horses with European shading and Chinese brushwork.

editions.name: Colorful Realm of Living Beings
editions.at: Museum of the Imperial Collections, Tokyo
editions.note: Thirty hanging scrolls of roosters, fish, insects and flowers, given to a Kyoto temple. Jakuchū used costly pigments and painted the back of the silk too, for richer color.

editions.name: The Swing
editions.note: A young woman kicks off her shoe at the top of the swing while her lover hides in the roses below. Pure Rococo flirtation, commissioned by a baron.

editions.name: Self-portrait in a Straw Hat
editions.note: Her answer to a Rubens portrait she saw in Antwerp, painted in open-air light. She became Marie Antoinette's portrait painter and one of the most successful artists of her time.
editions.credit: Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun · Public domain

editions.name: The Death of Marat
editions.at: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels
editions.note: The revolutionary journalist murdered in his bath, painted by his friend weeks later like a martyred saint. The whole top half is an empty wall.

editions.name: Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss
editions.note: Cupid lands to wake the sleeping Psyche with a kiss, their arms making a ring around their faces. Meant to be walked around.

editions.name: The Third of May 1808
editions.note: A French firing squad shooting Madrid rebels; the man in the white shirt throws his arms up like Christ. Often called the first modern painting of war.

editions.name: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
editions.note: A man seen from behind on a rocky peak over the fog. The back view lets you stand in his place, a favorite move of Friedrich's.

editions.name: The Hay Wain
editions.note: A horse cart in the river by Flatford Mill in Suffolk, the countryside where Constable grew up. Ignored in London, it won a gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824.

editions.name: Liberty Leading the People
editions.note: Liberty in a red cap leads Parisians over the barricades in the July Revolution of 1830. The boy waving pistols may have inspired Gavroche in Les Misérables.

editions.name: The Fighting Temeraire
editions.note: An old warship from Trafalgar towed by a small black steam tug to be broken up, under a burning sunset. Turner called it his darling and never sold it.
editions.credit: J. M. W. Turner · Public domain

editions.name: Queen Mother Pendant Mask
editions.note: A small ivory mask of Idia, mother of Oba Esigie, worn at the king's hip in ceremonies. The tiny heads in her crown are Portuguese traders. Taken by British troops in 1897; Nigeria has asked for these masks back.

editions.name: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake
editions.note: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo: people hurry across a bridge in rain drawn as fine dark lines. Van Gogh copied it in oils in 1887.

editions.name: Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket
editions.note: Fireworks over a London pleasure garden at night, nearly abstract. The critic John Ruskin accused Whistler of flinging a pot of paint in the public's face; Whistler sued and won one farthing.

editions.name: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
editions.note: A barmaid looks out past you while the mirror behind her shows the music hall crowd and a man talking to her. The reflection doesn't quite add up, on purpose. Manet's last major painting.

editions.name: Impression, Sunrise
editions.note: The port of Le Havre in morning haze with a small orange sun. A critic mocked the title, and the whole movement got its name.

editions.name: Water Lilies
editions.note: Huge panels of his pond at Giverny, hung in two oval rooms so they wrap around you. Monet offered them to France the day after the 1918 armistice.

editions.name: Bal du moulin de la Galette
editions.note: A Sunday afternoon dance in Montmartre, sunlight falling through the trees in spots on the crowd. Renoir's friends posed as the dancers.

editions.name: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen
editions.at: The Met, New York (bronze cast; the wax original is in Washington)
editions.note: A ballet student, first made in wax with a real cotton tutu, a silk ribbon and real hair. Critics found it shockingly lifelike. The only sculpture Degas ever showed; the bronzes were cast after he died.

editions.name: Paris Street; Rainy Day
editions.note: A wide new Paris crossroads in the rain, couples under umbrellas cut off at the edges like a snapshot. Caillebotte was a painter and a rich collector who bought his friends' work.

editions.name: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
editions.note: Parisians resting by the Seine, built from tiny dots of pure color that mix in your eye. Seurat worked on it for two years.

editions.name: The Basket of Apples
editions.note: A tipped basket, a bottle and biscuits on a table whose edges don't line up, as if seen from several places at once. The kind of picture that led to Cubism.

editions.name: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
editions.note: Painted in Tahiti and read right to left, from a baby to an old woman near death. Gauguin thought of it as his testament.

editions.name: Almond Blossoms
editions.note: Branches of white blossom against a blue sky, painted to celebrate the birth of his nephew, named Vincent after him. He borrowed the look from Japanese prints.

editions.name: The Scream
editions.note: Munch wrote of feeling an endless scream pass through nature as the sky over the Oslo fjord turned blood red. He made several versions; this is the first painted one.

editions.name: Self-Portrait with Physalis
editions.note: A sharp, sideways self-portrait with a sprig of orange lantern fruit. Schiele painted himself again and again before he died of the 1918 flu at 28.

editions.name: The Thinker
editions.note: First made as Dante sitting above The Gates of Hell, then enlarged on its own. More than twenty full-size casts stand around the world.

editions.name: The Waltz
editions.note: Two dancers spinning off balance, her dress swirling into a wave. The ministry first refused the nude version as too sensual, so Claudel added the drapery.

editions.name: Moulin Rouge: La Goulue
editions.note: His first poster, for the Moulin Rouge: the dancer La Goulue kicking up her skirts, her partner a shadow in front. Pasted all over Paris, it made him famous overnight.

editions.name: The Child's Bath
editions.note: A mother washing a child's feet, seen from above, with the flat space and patterns of the Japanese prints Cassatt collected. She was the only American in the Impressionist shows.

editions.name: Madame X
editions.note: A Paris society beauty in black against brown. At the 1884 Salon a strap slipped off her shoulder caused such a scandal that Sargent repainted it and soon left for London.

editions.name: The Sleeping Gypsy
editions.note: A lion sniffs a sleeping mandolin player in the desert under a full moon. Rousseau was a self-taught customs clerk; Picasso threw a banquet in his honor.

editions.name: Dance
editions.note: Five red dancers in a ring on green and blue, made for the Moscow stairway of the collector Sergei Shchukin. Three colors and nothing else.

editions.name: Guernica
editions.note: His answer to the bombing of the Basque town by German and Italian planes, painted in about five weeks in black, white and gray. It waited at MoMA until Spain was a democracy and came to Madrid in 1981.

editions.name: Portrait of Pablo Picasso
editions.note: Gris's homage to the friend who invented Cubism with Braque, holding a palette and broken into tidy facets. Gris made Cubism more orderly.

editions.name: Composition VII
editions.note: His most complex painting before the war: colors and shapes swirling around a dark center, painted in a few days after months of studies. He thought of painting as music.

editions.name: Black Square
editions.note: A black square on white, first hung high in a room corner, where Russian homes keep an icon. Malevich called it the zero of form. X-rays found earlier pictures under the cracked black.

editions.name: Broadway Boogie Woogie
editions.note: Painted in New York, where he arrived in 1940 and fell for jazz: the black lines of his grids became yellow streets blinking with red, blue and gray.

editions.name: The Ten Largest, No. 7, Adulthood
materials: tempera on paper mounted on canvas
editions.note: One of ten huge paintings about the stages of life, made years before Kandinsky's first abstractions. She asked that her abstract work stay unseen for 20 years after her death.

editions.name: The Large Blue Horses
editions.note: Three blue horses folding into the hills. For Marc, blue was the color of the spiritual. A founder of the Blue Rider group, he was killed at Verdun in 1916.

editions.name: Street, Dresden
editions.note: Shoppers on a Dresden street in acid pink and orange, their faces like masks. Kirchner reworked it about ten years later.

editions.name: Senecio
editions.note: A round face built from squares of warm color, one eyebrow raised. Painted while Klee was teaching at the Bauhaus.

editions.name: Fountain
editions.at: Original lost; replicas in several museums
editions.note: A store-bought urinal laid on its back and signed R. Mutt, sent to an open show in New York that then hid it. The original was lost; it's known from Alfred Stieglitz's photograph.

editions.name: Bird in Space
editions.note: Not a bird but its flight: a tall polished blade with no wings or feathers. When one was shipped to the US in 1926, customs taxed it as metal, not art; Brâncuși sued and won.

editions.name: Nu couché
editions.note: From the nudes whose 1917 show in Paris was shut down by the police on opening day. In 2015 it sold for about $170 million.

editions.name: Black Iris
editions.note: A single iris so close up it fills the canvas. O'Keeffe said she painted flowers big so busy New Yorkers would take the time to look.

editions.name: Nighthawks
editions.note: A late-night diner with no door you can see, four people under fluorescent light. Hopper said that, maybe without meaning to, he was painting the loneliness of a big city.

editions.name: American Gothic
editions.note: A farmer and a woman (his daughter, Wood said) in front of an Iowa house with a Gothic window. The models were Wood's dentist and his sister.

editions.name: Detroit Industry Murals
editions.note: Twenty-seven fresco panels covering a courtyard: the Ford River Rouge plant as a giant machine of workers and steel. Rivera thought it his best work.

editions.name: Abaporu
editions.note: A giant-footed figure with a tiny head beside a cactus and a sun like a lemon slice. A birthday gift to her husband, the poet Oswald de Andrade, it sparked his Anthropophagic Manifesto. At MALBA since 2001.

editions.name: América Invertida
editions.note: South America drawn upside down, the South Pole on top. Our north is the south, Torres-García wrote, calling for a Latin American art of its own.

editions.name: Manifestación
editions.note: A crowd of out-of-work people under a banner asking for bread and work, faces painted from photographs. Berni painted it on burlap sacking.

editions.name: Three Girls
editions.at: National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi
editions.note: Three young women waiting in silence, painted after Sher-Gil came back to India from Paris. It won a gold medal in Bombay in 1937. She died at 28.

editions.name: Shakuntala
editions.note: Shakuntala pretends to pull a thorn from her foot so she can look back at the king she loves. Ravi Varma's prints of Hindu epics hung in homes all over India.

editions.name: The Migration Series, Panel 1
editions.note: Sixty small panels on the Great Migration of Black Americans from the South to the North. Panel 1: a crowd at a train station. MoMA and the Phillips split the series, evens and odds.

editions.name: The Treachery of Images
editions.note: A pipe painted like a shop sign, with Ceci n'est pas une pipe written underneath. He's right: it's a picture of a pipe.

editions.name: The Persistence of Memory
editions.note: Melting pocket watches on a branch, a ledge and a strange sleeping creature, under the cliffs of Catalonia. It's only 24 by 33 cm.

editions.name: The Song of Love
editions.note: A marble head of Apollo, a rubber glove and a green ball nailed to a wall. Magritte said seeing it moved him to tears.

editions.name: Snow at Zōjō Temple
editions.note: A woman with an umbrella in falling snow passes the red gate of a Tokyo temple. Hasui led the revival of the woodblock print and was named a Living National Treasure.

editions.name: The Cradle
editions.note: Her sister Edma watching her baby sleep behind a sheer veil. Shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874, where Morisot was the only woman.

editions.name: Gismonda
editions.note: A life-size poster for Sarah Bernhardt in Gismonda, done in a rush over Christmas. She signed him to a six-year contract, and the Mucha style was born.

editions.name: Interior with Young Woman Seen from the Back
editions.note: His wife Ida from behind in their quiet gray Copenhagen apartment. Hammershøi painted the same rooms for years, nearly empty.

editions.name: Barge Haulers on the Volga
editions.note: Eleven men in harness drag a barge upriver in the heat. Repin met real haulers on the Volga and painted them one by one.

editions.name: Walk on the Beach
editions.note: His wife and daughter in white on the beach at Valencia, veils lifting in the wind. Sorolla painted outdoors, fast, chasing Mediterranean light.

editions.name: The Gulf Stream
editions.note: A man alone on a broken boat, sharks circling and a waterspout behind. Asked about the ending, Homer said the man would be rescued.

editions.name: The Banjo Lesson
editions.note: An old man teaching a boy the banjo by firelight, painted against the minstrel clichés of the time. Tanner became the first African American painter with international fame.

editions.name: Shrimp
editions.note: Translucent shrimp in a few wet strokes of ink, the subject he's most loved for. Qi Baishi kept shrimp in a bowl by his desk to study them.

editions.name: The Jungle
materials: gouache on paper mounted on canvas
editions.note: Mask-faced figures among sugar cane, a Cuban answer to Picasso's African masks. Lam wanted it shown in New York to bring Afro-Cuban culture into modern art.

editions.name: Christ the Redeemer
editions.note: 30 m tall on top of Corcovado mountain, arms 28 m wide. Designed with the engineer Heitor da Silva Costa; the face is by Gheorghe Leonida. Its skin is a mosaic of soapstone triangles.

editions.name: Statue of Liberty
editions.note: A gift from France: thin hammered copper over an iron frame designed by Gustave Eiffel, shipped in 350 pieces. The copper had turned green by around 1906.

editions.name: Lobster Trap and Fish Tail
materials: painted steel wire and sheet aluminum
editions.note: A mobile made for the stairwell of MoMA's new building, turning in the air. Marcel Duchamp gave Calder's moving sculptures their name: mobiles.

editions.name: Simultaneous Windows on the City
editions.note: Paris seen through panes of prism color, the Eiffel Tower a green shape in the middle. The poet Apollinaire called this colorful Cubism Orphism.

editions.name: Christ's Entry into Brussels in 1889
editions.note: Christ on a donkey almost lost in a masked carnival crowd. Too much for Ensor's own art group, which refused to show it; he kept it in his studio for decades.

editions.name: Recumbent Figure
editions.note: A woman lying like a landscape, hollowed through, carved in brown Hornton stone for the garden of a modernist house in Sussex.

editions.name: Autumn Rhythm (Number 30)
editions.note: Paint dripped and flung onto canvas laid on the barn floor, Pollock moving all around it. More than 5 m wide. I am nature, he said.

editions.name: Woman I
editions.note: A grinning woman with huge eyes, torn out of slashing brushwork. De Kooning fought with it for about two years and nearly gave it up.

editions.name: Mountains and Sea
editions.note: Thinned paint poured onto raw canvas on the floor so it soaked in like watercolor, after a trip to Nova Scotia. Her soak-stain method opened the way to Color Field painting.

editions.name: Vir Heroicus Sublimis
editions.note: More than 5 m of red split by five thin vertical stripes he called zips. Newman wanted it seen up close, so the red is all you see.

editions.name: Study after Velázquez's Portrait of Pope Innocent X
editions.note: Velázquez's pope screaming behind a curtain of streaks, caged in a glass box. Bacon worked from reproductions and never went to see the original in Rome.

editions.name: Campbell's Soup Cans
editions.note: Thirty-two canvases, one for each flavor Campbell's sold. At their first show in Los Angeles they stood on a shelf like in a grocery store, $100 each.

editions.name: Whaam!
editions.note: One fighter jet blowing up another, enlarged from a 1962 war comic across two canvases, Ben-Day dots and all.

editions.name: A Bigger Splash
editions.note: A California pool, a flat modern house and the splash of someone who just went under. Hockney liked that a splash lasts two seconds and took him two weeks to paint.

editions.name: Friendship
materials: gold leaf and oil on canvas
editions.note: A square of gold leaf with a fine grid scored into it. Martin painted grids for decades and said they were about innocence and joy.

editions.name: IKB 191
materials: pigment and synthetic resin on canvas
editions.note: One flat field of International Klein Blue, the matte ultramarine he registered in 1960. Klein wanted pure color with nothing in the way.

editions.name: Spatial Concept, Waiting
editions.note: One clean slash through a painted canvas, opening the picture onto the space behind it. Fontana, born in Rosario, Argentina, made his first cuts in 1958 and kept making them for the rest of his life.

editions.name: Betty
editions.note: His daughter turning away in a red and white jacket, painted from a photo he took when she was 11. She's looking back into one of his gray paintings.

editions.name: Untitled (Skull)
editions.note: A huge head that's half X-ray, half mask, painted when Basquiat was 20 and leaving graffiti behind for canvas.

editions.name: Flag
materials: oil and collage on fabric on plywood
editions.note: Johns said he dreamed of painting the American flag. Built from wax paint over newspaper scraps you can still read, it's a flag and a painting at once.

editions.name: Monogram
editions.note: A stuffed goat with a car tire around its middle, standing on a painted platform. Rauschenberg called these painting-sculpture hybrids combines.

editions.name: Movement in Squares
editions.note: A checkerboard that squeezes toward a fold, so the flat surface seems to buckle. Her black and white paintings made Riley the face of Op art.

editions.name: Chromosaturation
editions.at: Pérez Art Museum Miami (one of many)
editions.note: Rooms of pure red, green and blue light you walk through until your eyes adjust and start making up colors. Cruz-Diez, from Caracas, treated color as an event, not a coat of paint.

editions.name: Mona Lisa, Age Twelve
editions.note: Leonardo's sitter as a swollen child. MoMA showed it in 1961 and the Medellín painter's career took off. His figures aren't fat, he says: they're about volume.

editions.name: Violencia
editions.note: A dead pregnant woman lying as a gray landscape, about the years of La Violencia in Colombia. It won the national salon in 1962.

editions.name: Los suicidas del Sisga
editions.note: A newspaper photo of a couple who drowned themselves in the Sisga reservoir, posing just before, painted flat and bright like a cheap print. Pop art from Bogotá with a dark joke inside.

editions.name: Shibboleth
editions.note: A crack 167 m long running across the floor of Tate's Turbine Hall, about the divides of race and colonial history. It was filled in afterward; the scar is still there.

editions.name: The Parthenon of Books
editions.note: A full-size Parthenon covered in books banned under Argentina's dictatorship, put up on Avenida 9 de Julio after democracy came back. When it came down, people took the books home.

editions.name: Bicho
editions.note: Aluminum plates joined by hinges, meant to be handled and folded into new shapes. Clark called them critters; whoever picks one up finishes the work.

editions.name: La DS
editions.at: Centre national des arts plastiques, Paris
editions.note: A Citroën DS sliced lengthwise, its middle 62 cm taken out, and put back together as a car too narrow for two.

editions.name: Red Cube
editions.note: A red cube, or nearly, balanced on one corner in front of a black office tower in Lower Manhattan, with a hole bored through it.

editions.name: TV Buddha
editions.note: A statue of the Buddha watching itself live on a television, forever. Paik, born in Seoul, is often called the father of video art.

editions.name: Sunflower Seeds
editions.note: About 100 million porcelain sunflower seeds, each sculpted and painted by hand by some 1,600 artisans in Jingdezhen, poured across the Turbine Hall floor.

editions.name: Cloud Gate
editions.note: 168 steel plates welded and polished until the seams vanish, reflecting the Chicago skyline. Everyone calls it the Bean.

editions.name: Between Earth and Heaven
materials: aluminum bottle caps and copper wire
editions.note: Thousands of flattened liquor bottle caps stitched with copper wire into a shimmering hanging, like kente cloth in metal. It drapes differently every time it's hung.

editions.name: Tutu
editions.note: A portrait of the Ife princess Adetutu Ademiluyi, lost for decades and found in a London flat in 2017. In Nigeria it's called the African Mona Lisa.

editions.name: Napoleon Leading the Army over the Alps
editions.note: Jacques-Louis David's Napoleon on a rearing horse, with Napoleon replaced by a young man from Brooklyn in camouflage and Timberlands, against bright patterned wallpaper.

editions.name: Past Times
editions.note: A summer afternoon of Black families waterskiing and playing croquet, in the language of grand French leisure painting. It sold for $21.1 million in 2018, a record then for a living African American artist.

editions.name: Hot Spot
editions.note: A steel globe with every continent outlined in buzzing red neon, as if the whole planet were on alert. Hatoum was born in Beirut to a Palestinian family.

editions.name: The Physical Impossibility of Death in the Mind of Someone Living
editions.note: A 4 m tiger shark floating in a tank of formaldehyde. The first shark rotted and was replaced in 2006.

editions.name: Balloon Dog (Orange)
materials: mirror-polished stainless steel with transparent color coating
editions.note: A party balloon twisted into a dog, made 3 m tall in polished steel. There are five, each a different color; the orange one sold for $58.4 million in 2013.

editions.name: Love Is in the Bin
materials: spray paint and acrylic on canvas
editions.note: Girl with Balloon shredded itself halfway through its frame seconds after selling at Sotheby's in 2018, and got a new name. It sold again in 2021 for about 18 times the price.

editions.name: The Weather Project
editions.note: A giant half sun of yellow lamps doubled into a full one by a mirrored ceiling, in a misty Turbine Hall. People lay on the floor to find themselves up in the mirror. About two million came.

editions.name: Aten Reign
materials: LED and daylight in fabric rings
editions.note: The Guggenheim's rotunda filled with rings of slowly changing colored light under the skylight. Turrell works with light itself as his material.

editions.name: The Gates
materials: saffron nylon fabric on vinyl frames
editions.note: 7,503 saffron fabric gates along 37 km of Central Park paths, up for 16 days in February 2005. The artists paid for it themselves by selling their drawings.

editions.name: The Matter of Time
editions.note: Huge spirals and curves of rusted steel plate you walk through, the walls leaning in and out over your head.

editions.name: Angel of the North
editions.note: A 20 m steel angel with wings 54 m wide, on the site of an old coal mine above the main road north. Its wings tilt slightly forward, as if in an embrace.

editions.name: Walking Man
editions.note: A thin, rough bronze man mid-stride, once on the Swiss 100 franc note. A cast of Walking Man I sold for £65 million in 2010, then a record for any artwork at auction.

editions.name: Single Form
editions.note: A 6 m bronze slab with one hole, made in memory of her friend Dag Hammarskjöld, the UN Secretary-General killed in a plane crash in 1961.

editions.name: Tarot Garden
editions.note: Twenty-two giant figures from the tarot covered in mirror and ceramic on a Tuscan hillside. She lived inside The Empress for years while building it.

editions.name: Looped-wire sculptures
editions.note: Forms crocheted from one wire into lobes inside lobes, hung so their shadows draw a second sculpture on the wall. Asawa learned the loop from basket makers in Mexico in 1947.

editions.name: Sky Cathedral
editions.note: A wall of stacked boxes full of found wood, chair legs and finials, all painted black. Nevelson said black contains all colors.

editions.name: Untitled (Stack)
editions.note: Twelve identical green boxes up a wall, each gap as tall as a box. Judd disliked being called a minimalist and had his pieces made in factories.

editions.name: "Monument" for V. Tatlin
editions.note: Store-bought fluorescent tubes arranged like a stepped tower, a tribute to the Russian Constructivist Vladimir Tatlin. Flavin made 50 of these monuments over 26 years.

editions.name: Untitled (Portrait of Ross in L.A.)
editions.note: A pile of wrapped candies weighing 79 kg, his partner Ross's healthy weight before he died of AIDS. Visitors take a piece; the pile shrinks and is refilled.

editions.name: The Dance
editions.note: Couples and one woman alone dancing on a moonlit beach below a fortress. Rego, born in Lisbon, said the women are the same woman at different ages.

editions.name: The Snail
editions.note: Painted paper cut into squares that spiral like a shell, made when Matisse could no longer stand at an easel. Assistants pinned the pieces where he pointed.

editions.name: Earth's Creation
editions.note: Four panels of dense dabs of color, her country of Utopia after rain. Kngwarreye began painting on canvas in her late seventies and made thousands of works in eight years.
